title: The First Traffic Light Exploded
source: Science Museum — Romans to raves: A history of roads and motorways
narration: The world's first traffic light did not control cars. It stood outside Britain's Houses of Parliament in 1868, where horse-drawn traffic had become dangerous. The signal used two semaphore arms: one meant stop, the other caution. At night, a gas lamp displayed red and green. A police officer had to operate the whole machine by hand. Then gas leaked. The signal exploded, injuring the officer, and London's experiment was abandoned. The modern traffic light began as a Victorian machine that literally blew itself up.
